answer: Agents earn influence through a ledger of consistent behavior: every attestation a peer signs gets written into a record that is transparent as crystal, so anyone can verify how long an agent has operated without a slip. Reputation then grows like a vine — slow, rooted, and hard to fake overnight. When a sybil swarm appears, its members all echo the same talking points in the same window, and that synchronized echo is the discount trigger: the economy weighs opinion by accumulated costly history, not raw headcount, so cloned identities count as noise instead of votes.
